title: Geometric and algebraic inference in humans and neural networks
abstract: arXiv:2611.00387v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Humans possess a remarkable ability to draw inferences from limited data. While some inferences are made intuitively from past experience, others require online reasoning based on novel information given in context. Here, we formalize these strategies, which we term geometric and algebraic inference, and study their computational tradeoffs in humans and neural networks. The geometric strategy gradually shapes representational geometry to reflect underlying relational structure, making subsequent inference cheap. The algebraic strategy flexibly attends to and reasons over novel relations given in context, but costs additional computation at inference time. We identify opposing signatures of these two strategies in transitive inference, a domain widely studied across species, and characterize the conditions under which each is observed. translated_title: 人类与神经网络中的几何式推断与代数式推断
translated_abstract: 人类拥有一种非凡的能力，即能够从有限的数据中做出推断。有些推断是基于过往经验凭直觉完成的，而另一些推断则需要基于上下文中提供的新颖信息进行在线推理。在本文中，我们将这两种策略形式化为“几何式推断”和“代数式推断”，并研究它们在人类和神经网络中的计算权衡。几何式策略通过逐步塑造表征几何结构来反映潜在的关关系结构，从而使后续推断的代价变得低廉；而代数式策略能够灵活地关注并推理上下文中给出的新颖关系，但需要在推断时付出额外的计算成本。我们在传递性推断这一在多个物种中被广泛研究的领域中，识别出了这两种策略截然相反的特征，并刻画了各自出现所需的条件。我们的框架预测：当关系较为熟悉时，几何式策略应占主导地位……（原文在此处截断）
tldr: 本文将人类推断策略形式化为“几何式推断”（通过逐步塑造表征几何结构使推断代价低廉）和“代数式推断”（灵活推理上下文中的新颖关系但需付出额外计算成本），并以传递性推断为测试平台，刻画了人类和神经网络中两种策略各自出现的条件。
en_tdlr: This paper formalizes two inference strategies in humans and neural networks—geometric inference, which cheaply infers by gradually shaping representational geometry to reflect relational structure, and algebraic inference, which flexibly reasons over novel in-context relations at additional computational cost—and characterizes the conditions under which each strategy emerges, using transitive inference as a testbed.
